question: During the in-cab inspection, what air pressure range should the air gauge show at the point the air compressor builds pressure to governor cut-out, unless the manufacturer specifies otherwise?
explanation: The manual states the air compressor should build air pressure to governor cut-out at approximately 120-140 psi or as specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Gauge

question: When checking the ammeter/voltmeter gauge in the cab, what are you confirming?
choice_a: That gauges show the alternator and/or generator is charging, or that the warning light is off
choice_b: That the fuel gauge reads at least half full
choice_c: That the oil pressure gauge reads at its maximum
choice_d: That the coolant temperature gauge is in the red zone
explanation: The manual instructs checking that gauges show alternator and/or generator is charging, or that the warning light is off.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Ammeter/Voltmeter

question: According to the manual, what must be true of the windshield during inspection?
choice_a: It must be tinted appropriately for the weather
choice_b: It must be equipped with a rain sensor
choice_c: It must be clean with no illegal stickers, no obstructions, or damage to the glass
choice_d: It must have visible defrost lines across its surface
explanation: The manual states the windshield should be clean with no illegal stickers, no obstructions, or damage to the glass.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Mirrors and Windshield

question: Besides spare electrical fuses, what emergency equipment must be checked under the general Emergency Equipment item?
choice_a: Two red flags and a first aid kit
choice_b: One reflective triangle and a wool blanket
choice_c: A tire iron and a set of jumper cables
choice_d: Three red reflective triangles and 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares, plus a fire extinguisher that is properly charged and securely mounted
explanation: The manual requires checking for spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles and 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares, and a fire extinguisher that is properly charged and securely mounted.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Emergency Equipment

question: What must you verify about wiper arms and blades during the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: That they were replaced within the last six months
choice_b: That they are secure, not damaged, and operate smoothly, and that washers (if equipped) operate correctly
choice_c: That they are painted the same color as the vehicle
choice_d: That they only operate on the intermittent setting
explanation: The manual states to check that wiper arms and blades are secure, not damaged, and operate smoothly, and that windshield washers, if equipped, must operate correctly.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Wipers/Washers

question: Along with the turn signals, four-way flashers, and high beam headlight, which other dash indicator is specifically listed as something you must test?
choice_a: The Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) indicator
choice_b: The fuel level indicator
choice_c: The check engine light
choice_d: The cruise control indicator
explanation: The manual lists testing that dash indicators work for the left/right turn signal, four-way emergency flashers, high beam headlight, and Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) indicator.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Lights/Reflectors/Reflector Tape Condition (Sides & Rear)

question: What must you check regarding the horn during the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: That the horn's volume meets a specific decibel limit
choice_b: That the horn can only be tested while the vehicle is stopped
choice_c: That the air horn and/or electric horn work
choice_d: That the horn is disconnected before testing other systems
explanation: The manual simply instructs checking that the air horn and/or electric horn work.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Horn

question: What does the manual require you to test for the Heater/Defroster item?
choice_a: That the defroster clears the windshield within one minute
choice_b: That the heater fan has at least three speed settings
choice_c: That the heater only works when the engine is above idle
choice_d: That the heater and defroster work
explanation: The manual states simply to test that the heater and defroster work.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Heater/Defroster

question: How is the parking brake check performed, according to the manual?
choice_a: By listening for an audible click when the parking brake lever is engaged
choice_b: With air pressure built to governor cutout and the parking brake engaged, by gently trying to pull forward to check the parking brake will hold the vehicle
choice_c: By measuring the parking brake pedal travel with a ruler
choice_d: By disconnecting the air lines and observing brake chamber movement
explanation: The manual states that with air pressure built to governor cutout and the parking brake engaged, you check that the parking brake will hold the vehicle by gently trying to pull forward with the parking brake on.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Parking Brake Check

question: What happens if you fail to perform both components of the hydraulic brake check?
choice_a: You automatically fail the vehicle inspection test
choice_b: You receive partial credit but may continue
choice_c: You are simply asked to repeat the check later in the exam
choice_d: You receive only a verbal warning from the examiner
explanation: The manual states that failure to perform both components of the hydraulic brake check will result in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: In step 1 of the hydraulic brake check, after pumping the brake pedal three times and holding it down for five seconds, what should you observe?
choice_a: The pedal should slowly sink to the floor
choice_b: The pedal should spring back to its resting position
choice_c: The pedal should not move (depress) during the five seconds
choice_d: The pedal should feel noticeably spongy
explanation: The manual instructs pumping the brake pedal three times, then holding it down for five seconds, and states the brake pedal should not move (depress) during the five seconds.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: What happens if you fail to perform all three components of the air brake check correctly?
choice_a: The examiner allows you to retake only the failed component
choice_b: You lose points but can still pass overall
choice_c: Nothing, since the components are optional for most vehicles
choice_d: You automatically fail the vehicle inspection test
explanation: The manual states that failure to perform all three components of the air brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check (Air Brake Equipped Vehicles Only)

question: For a single vehicle, after holding the foot brake for one minute during the air brake leak-down test, how much can the air pressure drop and still pass?
choice_a: 1 pound
choice_b: No more than 3 pounds
choice_c: 4 pounds
choice_d: 6 pounds
explanation: The manual states you check the air gauge to see if pressure drops more than three pounds in one minute for a single vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check (Air Brake Equipped Vehicles Only)

question: For a combination vehicle, what is the maximum allowable air pressure drop when holding the foot brake for one minute during the leak-down test?
choice_a: Four pounds in one minute
choice_b: Three pounds in one minute
choice_c: Five pounds in one minute
choice_d: Eight pounds in one minute
explanation: The manual states pressure should not drop more than four pounds in one minute for a combination vehicle during this check.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check (Air Brake Equipped Vehicles Only)

question: While fanning off air pressure by rapidly applying and releasing the foot brake, the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, flag) should activate before air pressure drops below what level, unless the manufacturer specifies otherwise?
choice_a: 40 psi
choice_b: 45 psi
choice_c: 55 psi
choice_d: 65 psi
explanation: The manual states low air warning devices should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check (Air Brake Equipped Vehicles Only)

question: As you continue fanning off air pressure on a tractor-trailer combination vehicle, in what psi range should the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve close (pop out), unless the manufacturer specifies a different level?
explanation: The manual states that at a range between 20-45 psi on a tractor-trailer combination vehicle (or level specified by the manufacturer), the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve should close (pop out).
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check (Air Brake Equipped Vehicles Only)

question: How is the service brake check performed, according to the manual?
choice_a: Pull forward at 20 mph, apply the service brake hard, and check for wheel lock-up
choice_b: Pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service brake, and stop, checking that the vehicle does not pull to either side
choice_c: Reverse at 5 mph while applying the service brake
choice_d: Apply the parking brake while the vehicle is moving at highway speed
explanation: The manual instructs pulling forward at 5 mph, applying the service brake and stopping, checking that the vehicle does not pull to either side and that it stops when the brake is applied.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Service Brake Check

question: What must you check about the safety belt during the in-cab inspection?
choice_a: That it is securely mounted, adjusts and latches properly, and is not ripped or frayed
choice_b: That it retracts automatically within two seconds
choice_c: That it is a specific color matching the seat upholstery
choice_d: That it has an airbag warning label attached
explanation: The manual states to check that the safety belt is securely mounted, adjusts, latches properly, and is not ripped or frayed.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Safety Belt

question: What should you check regarding the steering box and hoses in the External Inspection section?
choice_a: That the steering box has a manufacturer sticker attached
choice_b: That the power steering fluid is a specific brand
choice_c: That the steering box is securely mounted and not leaking, with no missing nuts/bolts, and check for power steering fluid leaks or hose damage
choice_d: That the steering wheel has no more than one inch of free play
explanation: The manual instructs checking that the steering box is securely mounted and not leaking, looking for missing nuts and/or bolts, and checking for power steering fluid leaks or damage to power steering hoses.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.1 - Steering, Steering Box/Hoses

question: What should you inspect about the steering linkage's connecting links, arms, and rods?
choice_a: That they are painted to match the frame
choice_b: That they are covered by a manufacturer's warranty sticker
choice_c: That they weigh less than a specified maximum
choice_d: That they are not worn or cracked, and that joints and sockets are not worn or loose with no missing nuts, bolts, or cotter keys
explanation: The manual states to see that connecting links, arms, and rods from the steering box to the wheel are not worn or cracked, and that joints and sockets are not worn or loose and there are no missing nuts, bolts, or cotter keys.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.1 - Steering, Steering Linkage

question: What should you look for regarding leaf springs during the suspension inspection?
choice_a: That the springs are painted a specific safety color
choice_b: Missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs
choice_c: That the springs have a manufacturer date stamp
choice_d: That the springs are lubricated with grease weekly
explanation: The manual instructs looking for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs, as well as broken or distorted coil springs.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.2 - Suspension, Springs/Air/Torque

question: What should you check at the points where suspension mounts secure to the vehicle frame and axle(s)?
choice_a: Cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or damaged bushings, and broken, loose, or missing bolts, u-bolts, or other axle mounting parts
choice_b: That the mounts are painted to prevent rust
choice_c: That the mounts include a torque specification label
choice_d: That the mounts are replaced every 100,000 miles
explanation: The manual states to look for cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or damaged bushings, and broken, loose, or missing bolts, u-bolts, or other axle mounting parts.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.2 - Suspension, Mounts

question: What must be true of the shock absorbers during the suspension check?
choice_a: They must be a specific brand approved by the manufacturer
choice_b: They must be replaced annually regardless of condition
choice_c: They must be secure with no leaks
choice_d: They must be painted black
explanation: The manual states to see that shock absorbers are secure and that there are no leaks.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.2 - Suspension, Shock Absorbers

question: For manual slack adjustors, how much should the brake pushrod move when pulled by hand with the brakes released?
choice_a: Up to three inches
choice_b: Up to two inches
choice_c: It should not move at all
choice_d: Not more than one inch
explanation: The manual states that for manual slack adjustors, the brake pushrod should not move more than one inch (with the brakes released) when pulled by hand.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.3 - Brakes, Slack Adjustors and Pushrods

question: What should you verify about the brake chambers?
choice_a: That they are painted a distinct color from the frame
choice_b: That they are not leaking, cracked, or dented, are mounted securely, and have no loose or missing clamps
choice_c: That they are replaced every time tires are changed
choice_d: That they include a visible pressure gauge
explanation: The manual states to see that brake chambers are not leaking, cracked, or dented and are mounted securely, with no loose or missing clamps.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.3 - Brakes, Brake Chambers

question: For drum brakes that have openings allowing the brake lining to be seen from outside the drum, what must you check?
choice_a: That a visible amount of brake lining is showing
choice_b: That the lining is a specific color
choice_c: That the lining has a manufacturer stamp visible
choice_d: That the lining was replaced within the last year
explanation: The manual states that for drums with visible-lining openings, you check that a visible amount of brake lining is showing.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Brake Linings

question: What repair is specifically NOT allowed on rims, according to the manual?
choice_a: Replacement of valve stems
choice_b: Repainting
choice_c: Welding repairs
choice_d: Tightening of lug nuts
explanation: The manual states rims cannot have welding repairs, and to check rims for rust trails that may indicate the rim is loose on the wheel.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.4 - Wheels, Rims

question: What is the minimum tread depth requirement stated in the manual for steering axle tires compared to all other tires?
choice_a: 2/32 on steering axle tires, 4/32 on all other tires
choice_b: 6/32 on all tires regardless of position
choice_c: 8/32 on steering axle tires, 4/32 on all other tires
choice_d: 4/32 on steering axle tires, 2/32 on all other tires
explanation: The manual states to check for minimum tread depth of 4/32 on steering axle tires and 2/32 on all other tires.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.4 - Wheels, Tires

question: How must tire inflation be checked during the inspection, according to the manual?
choice_a: By kicking the tires to feel for firmness
choice_b: By using a tire gauge; you will not get credit for simply kicking the tires or using a mallet
choice_c: By striking the sidewall with a mallet and listening to the sound
choice_d: By visually estimating whether the tire looks low
explanation: The manual states to check for proper inflation by using a tire gauge, noting you will not get credit if you simply kick the tires or use a mallet to check for proper inflation.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.4 - Wheels, Tires

question: What should you check regarding hub oil/grease seals and axle seals?
choice_a: That they are not leaking, and if the wheel has a sight glass, that the oil level is adequate
choice_b: That they were installed within the last month
choice_c: That they are a specific manufacturer's brand
choice_d: That they make no noise when the wheel is spun
explanation: The manual states to see that hub oil/grease seals and axle seals are not leaking and, if the wheel has a sight glass, that oil level is adequate.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.4 - Wheels, Hub Oil Seals/Axle Seals

question: What must you check about the fuel tank(s) on the side of the vehicle?
choice_a: That the fuel level is at least half full
choice_b: That the fuel is a specific grade of diesel
choice_c: That tank(s) are secure, cap(s) are tight, and there are no leaks from tank(s) or lines
choice_d: That the tank has a visible capacity label
explanation: The manual states to check that tank(s) are secure, cap(s) are tight, and that there are no leaks from tank(s) or lines.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.5 - Side of Vehicle, Fuel Tank

question: For vehicles equipped with emissions after-treatment equipment, what must you check regarding the DEF (diesel exhaust fluid) tank?
choice_a: That the DEF tank is completely full
choice_b: That the DEF tank is empty and needs immediate refilling
choice_c: That the DEF level is exactly at the halfway mark
choice_d: That the DEF level is adequate, meaning more than 1/8th of a tank, and that the DEF indicator on the dash is working properly
explanation: The manual states to check that the DEF tank level is adequate (more than 1/8th tank) and that the DEF indicator on the dash is working properly.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.5 - Side of Vehicle, Exhaust System

question: What should you look for when inspecting the frame?
choice_a: A manufacturer's VIN sticker on the crossmember
choice_b: Cracks, broken welds, holes or other damage to the longitudinal frame members, cross members, box, and floor
choice_c: That the frame is rust-free with fresh paint
choice_d: That the frame has an aftermarket reinforcement kit
explanation: The manual instructs looking for cracks, broken welds, holes or other damage to the longitudinal frame members, cross members, box, and floor.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.5 - Side of Vehicle, Frame

question: According to the manual, what signs indicate a lug nut may be loose?
choice_a: Rust trails or shiny threads
choice_b: A slightly different torque wrench click sound
choice_c: The nut appearing slightly discolored
choice_d: The nut being a different brand than the others
explanation: The manual states to check that all lug nuts show no signs of looseness such as rust trails or shiny threads.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.6 - Rear of Vehicle, Lug Nuts

question: When checking the air and electric lines at the tractor/coupling, what should you listen and look for?
choice_a: Air leaks; hoses and electrical lines that are not cut, chafed, spliced, or worn so that steel braid shows through, and lines not tangled, pinched, or dragging
choice_b: A specific color-coded sequence for connecting the lines
choice_c: That the lines are the exact same length on both sides
choice_d: That the lines were manufactured within the last two years
explanation: The manual instructs listening for air leaks and checking that air hoses and electrical lines are not cut, chafed, spliced, or worn (steel braid should not show through), and are not tangled, pinched, or dragging against tractor parts.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.7 - Tractor/Coupling, Air/Electric Lines

question: When checking the kingpin/apron/gap area of the fifth wheel, what must you verify?
choice_a: That the kingpin is painted a bright color for visibility
choice_b: That the apron includes a manufacturer weight rating sticker
choice_c: That the release arm engages automatically without driver input
choice_d: That locking jaws hold the kingpin in place and it is not bent or damaged, the apron is not bent, cracked, or broken, and the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap
explanation: The manual states to explain that locking jaws hold the kingpin in place and that the kingpin is not bent or damaged, make sure the visible part of the apron is not bent, cracked, or broken, and check that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate (no gap).
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.7 - Tractor/Coupling, Kingpin/Apron/Gap

question: In addition to the standard emergency equipment, what additional emergency items must school bus drivers inspect?
choice_a: An extra set of keys and a flashlight
choice_b: An Emergency Kit and a Body Fluid Cleanup Kit
choice_c: A megaphone and a whistle
choice_d: A backup two-way radio
explanation: The manual states school bus drivers must also inspect an Emergency Kit and a Body Fluid Cleanup Kit, in addition to the standard emergency equipment.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.3 - School Bus Only, Emergency Kit / Body Fluid Cleanup Kit

question: What should you check about the trailer's landing gear during the side-of-trailer inspection?
choice_a: That it is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged
choice_b: That it is painted the same color as the trailer
choice_c: That it is lowered halfway for stability during inspection
choice_d: That it includes a digital pressure readout
explanation: The manual states to check that the landing gear is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged, and if power operated, to check for air or hydraulic leaks.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.4.2 - Side of Trailer, Landing Gear

question: What must you check about the glad hands at the front of the trailer?
choice_a: That they are painted red and blue
choice_b: That they are locked in place, free of damage or air leaks
choice_c: That they are the same brand as the tractor's
choice_d: That they are replaced every inspection cycle
explanation: The manual instructs making sure glad hands are locked in place, free of damage or air leaks, and that the trailer electrical plug is firmly seated and locked in place.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.4.1 - Trailer Front, Air/Electrical Connections

question: When inspecting the exterior of a coach/transit bus for level and air leaks, what should you check?
choice_a: That the vehicle has a functioning air conditioning system
choice_b: That the tires are inflated to the maximum sidewall rating
choice_c: That the vehicle is sitting level (front and rear), and if air-equipped, checking for audible air leaks from the suspension system
choice_d: That the baggage compartment lights turn on automatically
explanation: The manual states to see that the vehicle is sitting level (front and rear), and if air-equipped, check for audible air leaks from the suspension system.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.5.3 - External Inspection of Coach/Transit Bus, Level/Air Leaks

question: What should you check about the battery connections during the coach/transit bus external inspection?
choice_a: That connections are tight, cell caps are present, and connections do not show signs of excessive corrosion
choice_b: That the battery is less than one year old
choice_c: That the battery box is a specific color
choice_d: That the battery voltage reads exactly 12.6 volts
explanation: The manual states to see that battery(s) are secure, connections are tight, and cell caps are present, and that battery connections should not show signs of excessive corrosion.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.5.3 - External Inspection of Coach/Transit Bus, Battery/Box

question: According to the manual, what do all four versions of the Class A vehicle inspection test include?
choice_a: Only an inspection of the tires and brakes
choice_b: A written quiz followed by a road test
choice_c: An interview about vehicle maintenance history
choice_d: An engine start, an in-cab inspection, and an inspection of the coupling system
explanation: The manual states that all four versions of the Class A vehicle inspection test include an engine start, an in-cab inspection, and an inspection of the coupling system.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 - Class A Vehicle Inspection Test

topic: Class B and C Vehicle Inspection Test
question: According to the manual, what do all three versions of the Class B and C vehicle inspection test include?
choice_a: An engine start and an in-cab inspection
choice_b: A full coupling system inspection only
choice_c: A written exam on air brake theory
choice_d: A road test of at least 30 minutes
explanation: The manual states that all of the Class B and C vehicle inspection tests include an engine start and an in-cab inspection, and that the applicant will also have to inspect any special features of the vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 - Class B and C Vehicle Inspection Test

question: What does the manual say must happen before you can proceed to the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: You must first complete a written knowledge test
choice_b: You must first present your medical certificate
choice_c: You must first sign a liability waiver
choice_d: You must first pass the Vehicle Inspection test
explanation: The manual explicitly states that the Vehicle Inspection must be passed before you can proceed to the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.5.4 - Remainder of Coach/Transit Bus
